objects.title: Interval projection
objects.paper_statement: For real numbers \(a\leq b\), let \(\Pi_{[a,b]}:\mathbb R\to [a,b]\) be the interval projection \(\Pi_{[a,b]}(z)=\min\{b,\max\{a,z\}\}\).

objects.title: I.i.d. observed sampling
objects.paper_statement: For each observed law \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), let \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\) denote the observed triple for unit \(i\). The observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with common law \(\mathbb P\).

objects.title: Consistency of outcomes
objects.paper_statement:
The observed outcome satisfies
\[
Y=Y(A)
\]
almost surely.

objects.title: Conditional exchangeability
objects.paper_statement:
For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), the potential outcome \(Y(a)\) is conditionally independent of treatment given covariates:
\[
Y(a)\perp A\mid X .
\]

objects.title: Fixed overlap
objects.paper_statement:
Let \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be the finite covariate alphabet. For every observed law \(\mathbb P\) under consideration and every \(x\in[d]\) with covariate-cell mass \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)>0\), the treatment propensity \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) satisfies
\[
\epsilon\leq \pi_x \leq 1-\epsilon ,
\]
where \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) is the fixed overlap constant.

objects.title: Observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\)
objects.paper_statement:
For a full-data law \(P\), its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) is the law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) defined by
\[
\operatorname{Obs}(P)\{(x,a,y)\}
=
P(X=x,A=a,Y=y),
\qquad
(x,a,y)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^2.
\]

objects.title: Observed-law class \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\)
objects.paper_statement:
Under \cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}, let
\[
\Delta_d=\left\{p\in[0,1]^d:\sum_{x=1}^d p_x=1\right\}.
\]
The class \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) consists of all laws \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) for which there exist \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\Delta_d\), propensities \(\pi_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and means \(\mu_{ax}\in[0,1]\) such that, for every \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
q_{a1,x}
=
p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}\mu_{ax},
\qquad
q_{a0,x}
=
p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}(1-\mu_{ax}),
\]
where
\[
q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y).
\]
For each cell \(x\), write
\[
q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x}).
\]
The support contains at most \(d\) covariate cells, and on any null cell the parameters may be chosen arbitrarily within the displayed ranges.

objects.title: Observed-law optimal value \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\)
objects.paper_statement:
For \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}, with table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\), the observed-law optimal-regression functional is
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\Psi(\mathbf q)
:=
\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}.
\]
This value is independent of the permitted choice of \(\mu_{ax}\) on cells with \(p_x=0\).

objects.title: Minimax risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\)
objects.paper_statement:
The fixed-sample minimax squared risk is
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
:=
\inf_{\widehat V}
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
E_{\mathbb P}
\left[
\left\{
\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Psi(\mathbb P)
\right\}^2
\right],
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable maps
\[
\widehat V:\bigl([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\bigr)^n\to\mathbb R.
\]

objects.title: Full-data causal class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\)
Overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\)
objects.paper_statement:
The four-cell overlap cone is
\[
\mathcal C_\epsilon
:=
\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\leq s_1(u)\leq(1-\epsilon)s(u)\},
\]
where, for each \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1},
\qquad
s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u).
\]

objects.title: Global extension \(g_{a,\epsilon}\) and \(\bar f_\epsilon\)
objects.paper_statement:
For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with \(s(u)>0\), define the overlap-stabilized arm contribution
\[
g_{a,\epsilon}(u)
:=
\frac{s(u)u_{a1}}{\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}},
\qquad a\in\{0,1\},
\]
and the globally defined cellwise maximum contribution
\[
\bar f_\epsilon(u)
:=
\max_{a\in\{0,1\}} g_{a,\epsilon}(u).
\]
At the origin,
\[
g_{a,\epsilon}(0)=0,
\qquad
\bar f_\epsilon(0)=0.
\]

objects.title: Oracle value \(V^\star(P)\)
objects.paper_statement:
For a full-data law \(P\), the full-data causal optimal-treatment value is
\[
V^\star(P)
=
E_P\!\left[
\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}
E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}
\right].
\]

objects.title: Identification and completion
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(d\ge 2\), let \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and let \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}. Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Cell overlap.)} For every \(x\in[d]\), the four-vector \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) belongs to the overlap cone \(\mathcal C_\epsilon\) of \cref{obj:def:overlap-cone}.
\item \textbf{(Observed value.)} The observed-law optimal-regression value of \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} satisfies
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^d \bar f_\epsilon(q_x).
\]
\item \textbf{(Global extension bounds.)} For every \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\), the global extension of \cref{obj:def:global-extension} satisfies
\[
0\le \bar f_\epsilon(u)\le s(u).
\]
\item \textbf{(Global Lipschitz property.)} For every \(u,v\in\mathbb R_+^4\),
\[
\left|\bar f_\epsilon(u)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\right|
\le (1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}\left|u_{\jmath}-v_{\jmath}\right|.
\]
\item \textbf{(Completion.)} There exists a full-data law \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class} whose observed margin satisfies \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)=\mathbb P\). The completion is consistent and conditionally exchangeable, treatment is independent of the joint potential-outcome vector given \(X\), and the two potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables given \(X\).
\item \textbf{(Observed margins.)} For every full-data law \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\), its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) of \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Causal value identification
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(d\ge 2\), let \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), and let \(P\) be a full-data law satisfying \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Then the full-data oracle value in \cref{obj:def:oracle-value} agrees with the observed-law optimal-regression value in \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} evaluated at the observed margin in \cref{obj:def:observed-margin}:
\[
V^\star(P)=\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P)\}.
\]

objects.title: Empirical-ratio estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\)
objects.paper_statement:
For \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define the empirical counts
\[
\overline N_x
=
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=x\},
\qquad
\overline N_{ax}
=
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\},
\]
and
\[
\overline S_{ax}
=
\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}.
\]
Set
\[
\widehat p_x=\frac{\overline N_x}{n},
\qquad
\widehat\mu_{ax}=\frac{\overline S_{ax}}{\overline N_{ax}},
\]
with the convention \(0/0=0\). The empirical-ratio optimal-value estimator is
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}
=
\sum_{x=1}^d \widehat p_x \max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\widehat\mu_{ax}.
\]

objects.title: Treatment-outcome coordinate set
objects.paper_statement:
The treatment-outcome coordinate set \(\mathcal J\) is
\[
\mathcal J:=\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}.
\]
A coordinate index is denoted by \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).

objects.title: Jackson polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\)
objects.paper_statement:
For an integer \(K_d\ge 2\), define the order-four Jackson kernel on \([-\pi,\pi]\) by
\[
J_{K_d}(t)
=
c_{K_d}
\left\{
\frac{\sin(K_dt/2)}{\sin(t/2)}
\right\}^{4},
\]
with removable values filled continuously and normalizing constant \(c_{K_d}\) chosen so that
\[
\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} J_{K_d}(t)\,dt=1.
\]
For a rectangle
\[
Q_x
=
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}],
\]
define its coordinate centers and radii by
\[
b_{\jmath,x}
=
\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}
=
\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
The associated tensor polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) is defined by the even product convolution
\[
P_{x,K_d}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)
=
\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}
\bar f_\epsilon\{b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+t)\}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_{K_d}(t_{\jmath})\,dt.
\]

objects.title: Jackson-factorial estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\)
objects.paper_statement:
The inputs are \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), the alphabet size \(d\), and tuning constants \(D_0\), \(\kappa\), and \(H_0\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the logarithmic scale, Poissonized scale, and polynomial degree by
\[
L_d=\log(ed),
\qquad
m=\frac n8,
\qquad
K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor \kappa L_d\rfloor\}.
\]

\item If \(d<D_0\), output
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}.
\]
If \(d\ge D_0\) and \(n<d/L_d\), output
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
\frac12.
\]

\item In the remaining case, draw
\[
M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4).
\]
On the event \(M>n\), set
\[
\widetilde V=0.
\]

\item On the event \(M\le n\), draw independent marks
\[
B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,M.
\]
For each \(x\in[d]\) and coordinate \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), define pilot and evaluation counts
\[
N'_{\jmath,x}
=
\sum_{i=1}^M B_i\,\mathbf 1\{O_i\text{ belongs to coordinate }\jmath\text{ in cell }x\},
\]
and
\[
N_{\jmath,x}
=
\sum_{i=1}^M (1-B_i)\,\mathbf 1\{O_i\text{ belongs to coordinate }\jmath\text{ in cell }x\}.
\]

\item Define pilot frequencies and rectangle half-widths by
\[
c_{\jmath,x}
=
\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m},
\qquad
h_{\jmath,x}
=
H_0
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{c_{\jmath,x}L_d}{m}}
+
\frac{L_d}{m}
\right\}.
\]
Set
\[
\ell_{\jmath,x}
=
\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\},
\qquad
u_{\jmath,x}
=
c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x},
\]
and
\[
Q_x
=
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}].
\]
Let \(b_x\) and \(r_x\) denote the vector of coordinate centers and coordinate radii of \(Q_x\).

\item Expand the local polynomial as
\[
P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_\alpha
b_{x,\alpha}
\left(\frac{v-b_x}{r_x}\right)^\alpha .
\]
For \(h\ge 0\), define the centered factorial lift
\[
U_h(N;z)
=
\sum_{t=0}^h
\binom ht
(-z)^{h-t}
\frac{(N)_t}{m^t}.
\]

\item Define the clipping scale
\[
S_x
=
(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x},
\]
the unprojected cell estimate
\[
Z_x
=
\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
+
\sum_\alpha
b_{x,\alpha}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\frac{
U_{\alpha_{\jmath}}(N_{\jmath,x};b_{\jmath,x})
}{
r_{\jmath,x}^{\alpha_{\jmath}}
},
\]
and the clipped cell estimate
\[
T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
\Pi_{
[\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)-d^{1/4}S_x,\,
 \bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+d^{1/4}S_x]
}
(Z_x).
\]

\item Define the randomized projected aggregate by
\[
\widetilde V
=
\Pi_{[0,1]}
\left(
\sum_{x=1}^d T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}
\right).
\]
The all-data Rao--Blackwellized estimator is
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}
=
E\!\left[
\widetilde V
\mid
O_1,\ldots,O_n
\right],
\]
where the conditional expectation integrates only the auxiliary Poisson count \(M\) and marks \(B_1,\ldots,B_M\).
\end{enumerate}

objects.title: Fixed-law squared risk
objects.paper_statement: For an estimator \(\widehat V\) based on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) and an observed law \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), define \[ \operatorname{Risk}_{\mathbb P}(\widehat V,\Psi):=E_{\mathbb P^{\otimes n}}\left[\left\{\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Psi(\mathbb P)\right\}^2\right], \] where \(\mathbb P^{\otimes n}\) denotes the law of \(n\) independent observations each distributed as \(\mathbb P\).

objects.title: Jackson factorial risk bound
objects.paper_statement:
Assume the sampling condition in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}: for every alphabet size \(d\), sample size \(n\), and observed finite law \(\mathbb P\), the sample law is the canonical i.i.d. product law generated by \(\mathbb P\).

Then there exist tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(\kappa\in(0,1)\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\) such that the Jackson factorial estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\) of \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator} satisfies the following guarantee whenever:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Overlap.)} The overlap constant \(\epsilon\) satisfies \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} The sample size satisfies \(n\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} The alphabet size satisfies \(d\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Observed model.)} The observed law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}.
\end{itemize}
For every such \(\epsilon\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every such \(n,d\), and \(\mathbb P\),
\[
\operatorname{Risk}_{\mathbb P}
\left(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}},\Psi\right)
\le
C_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}.
\]
Here \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\) is the observed-law optimal-regression value of \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value}.

objects.title: \(L_1\) embedding \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\)
objects.paper_statement:
For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), define the observed atom masses
\[
q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=\frac{P_x}{4},
\qquad
q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=\frac{Q_x}{4},
\qquad x\in[d].
\]
Complete the observed law by taking the potential outcomes to be conditionally independent Bernoulli variables, setting the treatment propensity equal to \(1/2\), and imposing consistency.

objects.title: Fixed-sample two-sample \(L_1\) minimax risk
objects.paper_statement: Let \((Z_i,W_i)_{i=1}^n\) be independent paired observations with \(Z_i\sim\mathbf P\), \(W_i\sim\mathbf Q\), and \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\). The normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared error is \[ \mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}:=\inf_{\widehat D}\sup_{(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2}E_{\mathbf P,\mathbf Q}\left[\left\{\widehat D((Z_i,W_i)_{i=1}^n)-\|\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\|_1\right\}^2\right], \] where the infimum is over all measurable real-valued functions of the paired sample.

objects.title: Equal-propensity normalized \(L_1\) embedding
objects.paper_statement: For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), \(\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) is the full-data law on \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) with covariate mass \(p_x=(P_x+Q_x)/2\), treatment propensity \(\pi_x=1/2\), outcome regressions \(\mu_{1x}=P_x/(P_x+Q_x)\) and \(\mu_{0x}=Q_x/(P_x+Q_x)\) on cells with \(P_x+Q_x>0\), conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes with these means, treatment drawn independently of the potential outcomes given \(X\), and observed outcome \(Y=Y(A)\). Equivalently, its observed margin has cell masses \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\) and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\), with a consistency-compatible completion.

objects.title: Equal-propensity L1 reduction
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), let \(\mathbb P_0\) be an observed law on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), and let \(\mu_n\) be a law on \(n\) observed triples. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} The law \(\mu_n\) is the \(n\)-fold product law generated by \(\mathbb P_0\), as in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} \(2\le d\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap range.)} \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every pair \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), let
\[
\mathbb P=\operatorname{Obs}\{\mathrm{L1Emb}(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Obs}\) is the observed margin from \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} and \(\mathrm{L1Emb}\) is the \(L_1\) embedding from \cref{obj:synth_6}. The law \(\mathbb P\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}, and, for every \(x\in[d]\),
\[
p_x=\frac{P_x+Q_x}{2}.
\]
Moreover, whenever \(p_x>0\),
\[
\pi_x=\frac12,
\]
and the observed-law optimal-regression value from \cref{obj:def:observed-optimal-value} satisfies
\[
\Psi(\mathbb P)=\frac12+\frac14\sum_{x\in[d]} |P_x-Q_x|.
\]
Finally, the explicit fixed-\(n\) product Markov kernel obtained by applying the single-observation \(L_1\) embedding kernel independently across the \(n\) coordinates transforms the fixed paired-sample law generated by \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\) exactly into the product law \(\mathbb P^{\otimes n}\). Consequently, for the fixed-sample minimax squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk},
\[
\frac{1}{16}\,\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\le \mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon},
\]
where \(\mathfrak R^{L_1}_{n,d}\) is the normalized two-sample \(L_1\) minimax mean-squared risk.

objects.title: Global minimax lower bound
objects.paper_statement:
Suppose the observed samples satisfy the independent product sampling law in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}. For every overlap constant \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exists a constant \(c_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n\geq 1\) and \(d\geq 2\), the fixed-sample minimax squared risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
c_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}.
\]

external_dependencies.statement:
For every even integer \(K\), let \(E_K=\inf_{p:\deg(p)\leq K}\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\lvert\lvert tvert-p(t)vert\).  There exist symmetric probability measures \(
u_{0,K}\) and \(
u_{1,K}\) on \([-1,1]\) whose moments agree through degree \(K\) and such that \(\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{1,K}-\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{0,K}=2E_K\).  Moreover, there are universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c/K\leq E_K\leq C/K\).

external_dependencies.locator: Theorem 3, equation (24), and its Poissonized lower-bound proof
external_dependencies.statement: There are positive universal constants such that, whenever \(d\geq2\), \(n\) is at least a constant multiple of \(d/\log(ed)\), and \(\log(en)\) is at most a constant multiple of \(\log(ed)\), the minimax mean-squared error for estimating \(\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1\) from two independent samples of respective sizes \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\), one from each of \(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q\in\Delta_d\), is bounded below by a positive constant multiple of \(\min\{1,d/[n\log(en)]\}\).

objects.title: Matched minimax frontier
objects.paper_statement:
There are universal tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(0<\kappa<1\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\) for the Jackson factorial estimator such that the following holds.  For every fixed overlap constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there are real constants \(c_\epsilon\) and \(C_\epsilon\) with
\[
0<c_\epsilon\leq C_\epsilon .
\]
For every \(n\geq 1\) and \(d\geq 2\), with \(L_d=\log(ed)\) and with \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) denoting the fixed-sample observed minimax squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk},
\[
c_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{nL_d}\right\}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\leq
\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}
E_{\mathbb P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
  \left(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P)\right)^2
\right]
\leq
C_\epsilon \min\left\{1,\frac{d}{nL_d}\right\}.
\]
Moreover, the fixed-sample minimax squared risk over the full-data causal completion class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) is exactly \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) for the same \(n\), \(d\), and \(\epsilon\).

objects.title: Causal minimax risk
objects.paper_statement: For \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge2\), and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), write \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)^{\otimes n}\) for the law of \(n\) independent observations each distributed as the observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\), and define the observed-sample causal minimax squared risk by \[ \mathfrak R^{\mathrm{causal}}_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}} E_{\operatorname{Obs}(P)^{\otimes n}}\left[\left\{\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-V^\star(P)\right\}^2\right], \] where the infimum is over all measurable maps from \(([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)^n\) to \(\mathbb R\).

objects.title: Consistency and parametric boundaries
objects.paper_statement:
For every overlap constant \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), and for every alphabet-size sequence \(d_\bullet=(d_n)_{n\ge 1}\) satisfying \(d_n\ge 2\) for all \(n\), the following equivalences hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observed consistency.)} The fixed-sample minimax squared risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\) of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\longrightarrow 0
\]
if and only if
\[
d_n=o\{n\log(en)\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Causal consistency.)} The causal minimax squared risk over \(\mathcal P_{d_n,\epsilon}\) satisfies
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{causal}}_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\longrightarrow 0
\]
if and only if
\[
d_n=o\{n\log(en)\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed parametric boundary.)} The observed minimax risk sequence has the parametric \(n^{-1}\) rate, meaning that there exist constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\frac{c}{n}\le \mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\le \frac{C}{n},
\]
if and only if the alphabet-size sequence is uniformly bounded asymptotically, meaning \(d_n=O(1)\).
\item \textbf{(Causal parametric boundary.)} The causal minimax risk sequence has the parametric \(n^{-1}\) rate, meaning that there exist constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\frac{c}{n}\le \mathfrak R^{\mathrm{causal}}_{n,d_n,\epsilon}\le \frac{C}{n},
\]
if and only if \(d_n=O(1)\).
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Parent minimax reduction
objects.paper_statement:
There exist tuning constants \(H_0>0\), \(\kappa\in(0,1)\), and an integer cutoff \(D_0>2\), used by the Jackson factorial estimator in \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Matched frontier.)} For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there are constants \(c\) and \(C\) with \(0<c\leq C\) such that, for every \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\),
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{\sqrt d}{n}+\frac{d}{n\log(en)}\right\}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\leq
C\frac{d}{n}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Bounded alphabets.)} For every \(n\), every \(2\leq d<D_0\), every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\), and every observed sample, the Jackson factorial estimator in \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator} equals the empirical-ratio estimator in \cref{obj:def:empirical-ratio-estimator}:
\[
\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Bounded-alphabet sequences.)} For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\) and every sequence \(d_n\) with \(d_n\geq2\) for all \(n\) and \(d_n\leq d_{\max}\) for some finite \(d_{\max}\), there are constants \(c\) and \(C\) with \(0<c\leq C\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\frac{c}{n}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d_n,\epsilon}
\leq
\frac{C}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Constant route \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\)
objects.paper_statement: The route \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\) rescales the pilot-local four-cell rectangles by their Poisson noise geometry, optimizes the tensor-polynomial bias--variance functional for \(\bar f_\epsilon\), and dualizes the approximation constraint into moment-matched observed laws in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for the target \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\).

objects.title: Sharp overlap constant
objects.paper_statement:
A natural next question is whether, along each nonsaturated sequence with \(d\to\infty\) and
\[
\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\to0,
\]
the normalized risk
\[
\frac{n\log(ed)}{d}\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\]
converges to a finite positive limit, and whether an estimator attaining that limit can be derived through \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\).

objects.title: Tensor Jackson coefficient envelope
objects.paper_statement:
With the Jackson kernel notation of \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}, assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Order.)} \(K\ge 1\) is an integer.
\item \textbf{(Function.)} \(f\) is continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^{\mathcal J}\), where \(\mathcal J\) is the four arm-outcome coordinate set.
\item \textbf{(Envelope.)} \(B\ge 0\) and \(\lvert f(z)\rvert\le B\) for every \(z\in[-1,1]^{\mathcal J}\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a polynomial \(\mathcal R\) in the four normalized coordinates such that, for every angle vector \(\varphi:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
\mathcal R(\cos\varphi)
=
\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^{\mathcal J}}
f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_K(\tau_\jmath)\,d\tau .
\]
Here cosine is applied coordinatewise. Moreover, every multi-index \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R)\) satisfies
\[
\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\omega\in\mathcal J,
\]
the total degree of \(\mathcal R\) is at most \(8(K-1)\), and its coefficient one-norm satisfies
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R)}
\lvert \mathcal R_\beta\rvert
\le 2^{40K+20}B .
\]

objects.title: Jackson tensor extraction
objects.paper_statement:
Using the overlap-parameter notation of \cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}, let \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), let \(K\) be an integer, and let
\(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a four-coordinate rectangle with
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Overlap parameter.)} \(\epsilon>0\).
\item \textbf{(Radii.)} \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist a polynomial \(P_{x,K}\) in the four physical coordinates and a polynomial
\(\mathcal R_{x,K}\) in the four normalized coordinates such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Physical degree.)} Every coordinate degree of \(P_{x,K}\) is at most \(2(K-1)\).
\item \textbf{(Normalized degree.)} Every \(\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\) satisfies
\(\beta_\omega\le 2(K-1)\) for every coordinate \(\omega\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Centered evaluation.)} For every four-coordinate vector \(v\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\mathcal R_{x,K}\left(\left\{\frac{v_\jmath-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right).
\]
Here \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the globally defined cellwise maximum contribution from
\cref{obj:def:global-extension}.
\item \textbf{(Jackson convolution.)} For every angle vector \(\vartheta:\mathcal J\to\mathbb R\),
\[
P_{x,K}\left(\left\{b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}\cos(\vartheta_\jmath)\right\}_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\right)
\]
equals the order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution from \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel} of
\(\bar f_\epsilon\) precomposed with the affine parametrization of \(Q_x\), evaluated at
\(\vartheta\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient envelope.)}
\[
\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})}
\left|(\mathcal R_{x,K})_\beta\right|
\le
2^{40K+20}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
\end{itemize}

objects.title: Tensor Jackson convolution operator $\mathcal J_K$
objects.paper_statement: For a positive integer $K$, let $J_K(t)=c_K\{\sin(Kt/2)/\sin(t/2)\}^4$ on $[-\pi,\pi]$, with the removable values filled in continuously and with $c_K$ chosen so that $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_K(t)\,dt=1$. For a finite coordinate dimension $D$ and a function $f:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R$, the order-$K$ tensor Jackson convolution is the operator $\mathcal J_K$ defined, for $\theta\in\mathbb R^D$, by \[ (\mathcal J_K f)(\cos\theta) := \int_{[-\pi,\pi]^D} f\{\cos(\theta+t)\}\prod_{i=1}^D J_K(t_i)\,dt, \] where cosine and addition are coordinatewise. Equivalently, the product kernel $\prod_{i=1}^D J_K(t_i)$ is normalized to have integral one over $[-\pi,\pi]^D$.

objects.title: Tensor Jackson modulus
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(D\) be a finite coordinate dimension, let \(K\) be a positive integer, and let \(f:\mathbb R^D\to\mathbb R\). Let \(L\ge0\), let \(a_i\ge0\) and \(b_i\ge0\) for each \(i\in[D]\), and fix an angle vector \(\varphi\in\mathbb R^D\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Kernel.)} The order-\(K\) tensor Jackson convolution is formed from the order-four Jackson kernel in \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}.
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} The function \(f\) is continuous on the normalized cube \([-1,1]^D\).
\item \textbf{(Weighted increment modulus.)} For every shift \(\tau\in\mathbb R^D\),
\[
\left|f\{\cos(\varphi-\tau)\}-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^D\left(a_i|\tau_i|+b_i\tau_i^2\right),
\]
where cosine is applied coordinatewise.
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\left|(\mathcal J_K f)(\cos\varphi)-f(\cos\varphi)\right|
\le
L\sum_{i=1}^D\left(\frac{32a_i}{K}+\frac{64b_i}{K^2}\right).
\]

objects.title: Simultaneous Jackson certificate
objects.paper_statement:
There is a universal constant \(A>0\) such that, for every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) with the following property. Let:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(K\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Rectangle.)} \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) have \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\le u_{\jmath,x}\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge 0\), and positive radii
\[
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}>0
\]
for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(P_{x,K}\) be the tensor Jackson polynomial associated with \(\epsilon\), \(K\), and \(Q_x\) in \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}. Then the same polynomial satisfies all of the following conclusions:
\[
\deg_{\jmath}(P_{x,K})\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\jmath\in\mathcal J .
\]
For every \(v\in Q_x\),
\[
\left|P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(v)\right|
\le
C_\epsilon
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left\{
\frac{\sqrt{(v_{\jmath}-\ell_{\jmath,x})(u_{\jmath,x}-v_{\jmath})}}{K}
+
\frac{r_{\jmath,x}}{K^2}
\right\}.
\]
There are a finite multi-index set \(\mathcal A_x\) and coefficients \(b_{x,\alpha}\) such that, for every \(v\),
\[
P_{x,K}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}
b_{x,\alpha}
\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left(\frac{v_{\jmath}-b_{\jmath,x}}{r_{\jmath,x}}\right)^{\alpha_{\jmath}},
\]
with
\[
\alpha_{\jmath}\le 2(K-1)
\qquad\text{for every }\alpha\in\mathcal A_x\text{ and every }\jmath\in\mathcal J,
\]
and
\[
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}|b_{x,\alpha}|
\le
A^K(1+\epsilon^{-1})
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}.
\]

objects.title: Bad pilot moment bound
objects.paper_statement:
Fix the four-coordinate set \(\mathcal J=\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\). Let \(q=(q_\jmath)_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\) have nonnegative coordinates, let \(m>0\), let \(L\ge 1\), and let \(t\in\{1,2,4\}\). Suppose the pilot counts \((N'_{\jmath})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\) are independent with
\[
N'_{\jmath}\sim \operatorname{Pois}(m q_\jmath),
\qquad \jmath\in\mathcal J .
\]
With \(H_0=1024\), define the normalized aggregate pilot score
\[
\Gamma(N')
=
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left[
\left|{N'_{\jmath}\over m}-q_\jmath\right|
+
H_0\left\{\sqrt{{N'_{\jmath}\over m}{L\over m}}+{L\over m}\right\}
\right],
\]
and define the self-normalized bad-pilot event
\[
\mathsf G^c
=
\left\{
\exists\,\jmath\in\mathcal J:
\left|{N'_{\jmath}\over m}-q_\jmath\right|
>
{H_0\over 4}
\left\{\sqrt{{N'_{\jmath}\over m}{L\over m}}+{L\over m}\right\}
\right\}.
\]
Then, with \(C_t=10^{80(t+1)}\),
\[
E\!\left[\Gamma(N')^t\mathbf 1_{\mathsf G^c}\right]
\le
C_t e^{-20L}
\left\{
\sqrt{{\left(\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}q_\jmath\right)L\over m}}
+
{L\over m}
\right\}^{t}.
\]

objects.title: Good-pilot event
objects.paper_statement: Fix a cell \(x\), four-cell mass vector \(q_x=(q_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), Poisson scale \(m>0\), alphabet logarithm \(L_d=\log(ed)\), pilot-radius constant \(H_0\), and pilot counts \((N'_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\). Put \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\) and \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\). The coordinatewise good-pilot event used for the pilot rectangle is \[\mathsf G_x:=\bigcap_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\left\{\left|\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m}-q_{\jmath,x}\right|\le \frac{h_{\jmath,x}}{4}\right\}.\]

objects.title: Good pilot radius bound
objects.paper_statement:
Fix \(m>0\), an integer \(d\ge 1\), pilot counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) for \(\jmath\) in the four-coordinate set \(\mathcal J\), and coordinate intensities \(q_\jmath\ge 0\).  Let \(L_d=\log(ed)\), set \(p_x=\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}q_\jmath\), and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be the canonical pilot rectangle of \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}, with radii
\[
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2}.
\]
Assume that the good-pilot event
\[
\mathsf G_x=\bigcap_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}
\left\{\left|c_{\jmath,x}-q_\jmath\right|\le \frac{h_{\jmath,x}}{4}\right\},
\qquad c_{\jmath,x}=\frac{N'_{\jmath,x}}{m},
\]
holds, where \(h_{\jmath,x}\) is the canonical pilot half-width in \cref{obj:def:jackson-factorial-estimator}.  Then
\[
\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} r_{\jmath,x}
\le
2\cdot 10^6
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x L_d}{m}}+\frac{L_d}{m}
\right\}.
\]

objects.title: Normalized coefficient envelope
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(\epsilon>0\) be the overlap parameter from \cref{obj:ass:fixed-overlap}, let \(K\ge2\) be an integer, and let \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) be a rectangle over the four outcome-arm coordinate set \(\mathcal J\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Ordered endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\le u_{\jmath,x}\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative lower endpoints.)} \(\ell_{\jmath,x}\ge0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\item \textbf{(Positive radii.)} With
\[
b_{\jmath,x}=\frac{\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\qquad
r_{\jmath,x}=\frac{u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x}}{2},
\]
one has \(r_{\jmath,x}>0\) for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(b_x=(b_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), let \(r_x=(r_{\jmath,x})_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\), and let \(P_{x,K}\) be the Jackson tensor polynomial attached to \(Q_x\) by \cref{obj:def:jackson-kernel}. Define
\[
\mathcal R_{x,K}(z)
=
P_{x,K}\bigl((b_{\jmath,x}+r_{\jmath,x}z_\jmath)_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\bigr)
-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)
=
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x} b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J} z_\jmath^{\alpha_\jmath},
\]
where \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is the global cell extension from \cref{obj:def:global-extension} and \(\mathcal A_x=\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal R_{x,K})\). Then
\[
\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_x}|b_{x,\alpha}|
\le
(2^{60})^{K}(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}r_{\jmath,x}.
\]
Moreover, every \(\alpha\in\mathcal A_x\) satisfies
\[
\alpha_\jmath\le 2(K-1)
\]
for every \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\).

objects.title: Pilot-failure contributions
objects.paper_statement: Fix a cell \(x\), a four-cell mass vector \(q_x\), Poisson scale \(m>0\), and Jackson tuning. Let \(\mathbb P_{m,q_x}^{\mathrm{pil,eval}}\) denote the product-Poisson law of the pilot and evaluation count vectors, and let \(\mathsf G_x\) be the coordinatewise good-pilot event used for the pilot rectangle in the Jackson--factorial construction. With \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\) denoting the clipped cell statistic built from the pilot and evaluation counts, define \[ \mathrm{PF}_{1,x}:=\int_{\mathsf G_x^c}\left|T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\right|\,d\mathbb P_{m,q_x}^{\mathrm{pil,eval}}, \qquad \mathrm{PF}_{2,x}:=\int_{\mathsf G_x^c}\left(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)\right)^2\,d\mathbb P_{m,q_x}^{\mathrm{pil,eval}}. \]

objects.title: Centered factorial pilot control
objects.paper_statement:
Assume the product experiment satisfies the i.i.d. sampling law in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.  There is a universal Jackson tuning with self-normalized Poisson pilot-radius constant, polynomial-degree constant \(\kappa=1/100000\), and cutoff \(D_0=3\).  For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) such that the following assertions hold for every \(n,d\), every observed law \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), and every positive sample size \(n\), whenever \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:observed-model-class}.  Set \(m=n/8\), let \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) be the four-coordinate cell vector, and let \(p_x\) be the marginal mass of cell \(x\).

In the uncapped marked experiment generated by
\[
M\sim \operatorname{Pois}(n/4)
\]
together with i.i.d. observations from \(\mathbb P\) and independent fair pilot/evaluation marks, the count \(M\) has law \(\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\).  The induced pilot/evaluation table has law equal to the product, over cells \(x\in[d]\) and coordinates \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), of two independent Poisson count arrays with coordinate means \(m q_{\jmath,x}\).  For each fixed cell \(x\), the marginal law of the pilot and evaluation counts in that cell is therefore
\[
\bigotimes_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\operatorname{Pois}(m q_{\jmath,x})
\otimes
\bigotimes_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}\operatorname{Pois}(m q_{\jmath,x}).
\]

For every cell \(x\), every fixed pilot table, every coordinate \(\jmath\in\mathcal J\), every \(z\in\mathbb R\), and every \(h,t\in\mathbb N\), conditional expectation over the evaluation counts satisfies
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[U_h(N_{\jmath,x};z)\mid N'\right]
=
(q_{\jmath,x}-z)^h
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[U_h(N_{\jmath,x};z)U_t(N_{\jmath,x};z)\mid N'\right]
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\{h,t\}}
\binom{h}{\ell}\binom{t}{\ell}\ell!
\left(\frac{q_{\jmath,x}}{m}\right)^\ell
(q_{\jmath,x}-z)^{h+t-2\ell}.
\]

With the same tuning, the clipped Jackson-factorial cell statistic \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\) obeys, uniformly over all cells \(x\in[d]\),
\[
\left|
\mathbb E T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}-\bar f_\epsilon(q_x)
\right|
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x}{mL_d}}+\frac{1}{mL_d}
\right\},
\]
\[
\operatorname{Var}(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}})
\le
C_\epsilon d^{1/16}
\left\{
\frac{p_x L_d}{m}+\frac{L_d^2}{m^2}
\right\},
\]
and the pilot-failure contributions satisfy
\[
\mathrm{PF}_{1,x}
\le
C_\epsilon
\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{p_x}{mL_d}}+\frac{1}{mL_d}
\right\},
\qquad
\mathrm{PF}_{2,x}
\le
C_\epsilon d^{1/16}
\left\{
\frac{p_x L_d}{m}+\frac{L_d^2}{m^2}
\right\}.
\]

objects.title: Poisson minimax risk
Dense contrast law
objects.paper_statement:
For an integer \(d\geq 2\) and a contrast vector \(\theta=(\theta_x)_{x\in[d]}\) with \(\theta_x\in[-1/2,1/2]\) for every \(x\in[d]\), define \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) as the full-data probability law on \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) whose atom at \((x,a,y,y_0,y_1)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^4\) is
\[
P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}(x,a,y,y_0,y_1)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{1}{2d}\, b_{(1-\theta_x)/2}(y_0)\, b_{(1+\theta_x)/2}(y_1),
& y=y_a,\\[0.8em]
0,
& y\neq y_a,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(y_a=y_1\) if \(a=1\) and \(y_a=y_0\) if \(a=0\), and \(b_\mu(1)=\mu\), \(b_\mu(0)=1-\mu\).

objects.title: Dense moment-matching construction
objects.paper_statement:
For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), the overlap parameter, a dense domain certificate
\[
2\le d,\qquad
0<\epsilon,\qquad
\epsilon<\frac12,\qquad
0<a_{n,d}\le \frac12,
\]
and a dense prior family \(K\mapsto(\nu_{0,K},\nu_{1,K})\) indexed by positive even degrees, define the dense moment-matching construction as follows.  For every positive even \(K\), the family carries the prior-pair conditions that \(\nu_{0,K}\) and \(\nu_{1,K}\) are probability measures supported on \([-1,1]\), are symmetric, have matching moments through degree \(K\), and satisfy
\[
\int_{-1}^1 |t|\,d\nu_{1,K}(t)
-
\int_{-1}^1 |t|\,d\nu_{0,K}(t)
=
2E_K .
\]
The construction has components:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dense law.)} For each \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the potential-outcome law induced by the dense full-data masses, equivalently \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+\theta_x)/2\), and \(\mu_{0x}=(1-\theta_x)/2\), with \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independent Bernoulli variables given \(X=x\), \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the potential outcomes, and \(Y=Y(A)\).
\item \textbf{(Approximation scale.)} The approximation degree and best even-degree approximation error are
\[
K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_d\rceil,
\qquad
E_K=\inf\left\{e\in\mathbb R:\exists p,\ \deg(p)\le K,\ 
\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\bigl||t|-p(t)\bigr|\le e\right\}.
\]
The construction uses \(E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}\).
\item \textbf{(Poisson intensity and amplitude.)} The one-cell Poisson intensity and dense contrast amplitude are
\[
\lambda_{n,d}=\frac{2n}{d},
\qquad
a_{n,d}=\sqrt{\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}{64\lambda_{n,d}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Coordinate priors.)} The coordinate priors are
\[
\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},
\qquad
\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Dense product priors.)} The priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) are the pushforwards into the dense contrast class of the restrictions of \(\nu_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) and \(\nu_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) to \([-1,1]^d\), under coordinatewise scaling by \(a_{n,d}\).
\item \textbf{(Observation mixtures.)} The mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) are the observation-kernel mixtures induced by \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\), with independent Poissonized sample size \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\).
\item \textbf{(Risk and separation.)} The risk component is the Poissonized minimax risk
\[
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}.
\]
The prior target-mean separation is
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
E_{\Pi_{1,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-
E_{\Pi_{0,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
The construction carries the supplied prior-pair certificate at degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\) and the identities
\[
K=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}},
\qquad
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}.
\]

objects.title: Dense amplitude range
objects.paper_statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(2\le d\) and \(d^2<n\). For the lower-bound contrast amplitude \(a_{n,d}\) defined in \cref{obj:def:dense-moment-matching-construction},
\[
0<a_{n,d}\le \frac12.
\]

objects.title: Total variation distance
objects.paper_statement: For probability laws \(\mathbb M_0\) and \(\mathbb M_1\) on a common measurable space, define \(\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_0,\mathbb M_1)=\sup_{B}\lvert \mathbb M_0(B)-\mathbb M_1(B)\rvert\), where the supremum ranges over measurable events \(B\).

objects.title: Dense likelihood tail
objects.paper_statement: For the dense lower-bound degree \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\), Poissonized cell intensity \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), and dense amplitude \(a_{n,d}\), define the dense likelihood tail by \[\operatorname{tail}_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}:=\sum_{r=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda_{n,d}a_{n,d}^2)^r}{r!}.\]

objects.title: One-cell dense likelihood ratio
objects.paper_statement: Fix a Poisson cell intensity \(\lambda\ge0\). Let \(R_+\) and \(R_-\) be the two sign counts in one dense cell, and let \(E_0\) denote expectation under the zero-contrast baseline law \(R_+,R_-\stackrel{\mathrm{ind}}{\sim}\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda/2)\). For \(\theta\in[-1,1]\), the one-cell likelihood ratio relative to this baseline is \[ L_\theta(R_+,R_-):=(1+\theta)^{R_+}(1-\theta)^{R_-}. \] In the dense lower bound, \(L_{\theta_x}\) applies this definition with the cell contrast \(\theta_x\) and \(\lambda=\lambda_{n,d}\).

objects.title: Dense moment matching lower bound
objects.paper_statement:
Suppose the product experiment satisfies the i.i.d. sampling law in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.  There is an integer cutoff \(D_0\geq2\) such that, for every overlap constant \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there is a constant \(c_\epsilon>0\) with the following property.  For all integers \(d,n\) satisfying \(d\geq D_0\) and \(d^2<n\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree and amplitude.)} The lower-bound degree and amplitude obey
\[
8L_d\leq K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}<8L_d+2,
\qquad
a_{n,d}^2=\frac{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}d}{128n},
\qquad
a_{n,d}\leq \frac12 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Dense observed submodel.)} For every \(\theta\in[-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\), the dense equal-mass contrast submodel \(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) has observed margin in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and satisfies, for every \(x\in[d]\),
\[
p_x=\frac1d,
\qquad
\pi_x=\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_{1x}=\frac{1+\theta_x}{2},
\qquad
\mu_{0x}=\frac{1-\theta_x}{2},
\]
with
\[
\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
=
\frac12+\frac{1}{2d}\sum_{x=1}^d|\theta_x|.
\]
\item \textbf{(Moment-matched priors and mixtures.)} The two dense product priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) and \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\), with induced Poissonized mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\), may be chosen so that their prior-mean separation satisfies
\[
\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}
=
a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}},
\qquad
0<\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\leq1,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d})
\leq
d\{\operatorname{tail}_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\}^{1/2}
\leq
d\left\{\frac{(e/64)^{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}}{1-e/64}\right\}^{1/2}
\leq\frac1{16}.
\]
Under each of the two product priors, the target is concentrated around its prior mean:
\[
\int
\left(\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-\mathbb E_{\Pi_{j,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}\right)^2
\,d\Pi_{j,n,d}(\theta)
\leq
\frac{a_{n,d}^2}{4d},
\qquad j\in\{0,1\},
\]
and
\[
\Pi_{j,n,d}\left(
\left|\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}
-\mathbb E_{\Pi_{j,n,d}}\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}\right|
>
\frac{\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}}{4}
\right)
\leq
\frac18,
\qquad j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(One-cell likelihood identity.)} For all contrasts \(\theta,\theta'\in\mathbb R\),
\[
E_0[L_\theta L_{\theta'}]
=
\exp(\lambda_{n,d}\theta\theta').
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently,
\[
c_\epsilon(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}})^2
\leq
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon},
\qquad
c_\epsilon\frac{d}{nK_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}
\leq
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon},
\]
and the fixed-sample and Poissonized risks satisfy
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}
\geq
\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}
-
\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}.
\]
In particular,
\[
c_\epsilon\frac{d}{nL_d}
\leq
\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}.
\]

external_dependencies.statement:

8f2e3bc95986f9f6.statement:
-- @realizes \(Y(a)\)(last two coordinates)

/-- A probability law on the full-data alphabet. -/
structure PotentialLaw (d : ℕ) where

36c36f84602d3a1a.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.ConditionalExchangeability
36c36f84602d3a1a.statement:
/-- Armwise finite conditional independence `Y(r) ⟂ A | X`, separately for each arm. -/
def ConditionalExchangeability {d : ℕ} (Q : PotentialLaw d) : Prop :=
  ∀ x r a ya,
    poArmAtom Q x r a ya * (∑ a' : Bool, ∑ y' : Bool, poArmAtom Q x r a' y') =
      (∑ a' : Bool, poArmAtom Q x r a' ya) *
        (∑ y' : Bool, poArmAtom Q x r a y')

91effbcd082ba7e6.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.Overlap
91effbcd082ba7e6.statement:
/-- Every occupied cell has propensity in the fixed overlap interval. -/
def Overlap {d : ℕ} (epsilon : ℝ) (P : DiscreteLaw d) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, 0 < cellMass P x →
    epsilon ≤ propensity P x ∧ propensity P x ≤ 1 - epsilon

967248d5bd732412.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.observedMarginal
967248d5bd732412.statement:
/-- Push a full-data law to its observed margin. -/
noncomputable def observedMarginal {d : ℕ} (Q : PotentialLaw d) : DiscreteLaw d where
  pmf := Q.pmf.map (fun z => (z.1, z.2.1, z.2.2.1))

8f74757fa4759f30.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.ObservedModelClass
8f74757fa4759f30.statement:
/-- The unrestricted observed finite-law class, restricted only by overlap. -/
structure ObservedModelClass (epsilon : ℝ) {d : ℕ} (P : DiscreteLaw d) : Prop where
  d_ge_two : 2 ≤ d -- @realizes \(d\)(alphabet size at least two)
  epsilon_pos : 0 < epsilon -- @realizes \(\epsilon\)(strictly positive)
  epsilon_lt_half : epsilon < 1 / 2 -- @realizes \(\epsilon\)(strictly below one half)
  overlap : Overlap epsilon P -- @realizes \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\)(membership by overlap)

150f17bf01bd9696.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.observedOptimalValue
150f17bf01bd9696.statement:
/-- The optimal-regression value, defined only on the published observed model class. -/
noncomputable def observedOptimalValue {d : ℕ} {epsilon : ℝ}
    (P : DiscreteLaw d) (_hP : ObservedModelClass epsilon P) : ℝ :=
  observedOptimalValueRaw P

c6baa6c07afc422d.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.minimaxRisk
c6baa6c07afc422d.statement:

32b5977f2e58c211.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.CausalCompletionClass
32b5977f2e58c211.statement:
/-- Consistent, exchangeable causal completions with an overlapping observed margin. -/
structure CausalCompletionClass (epsilon : ℝ) {d : ℕ} (Q : PotentialLaw d) : Prop where
  d_ge_two : 2 ≤ d -- @realizes \(d\)(alphabet size at least two)
  epsilon_pos : 0 < epsilon -- @realizes \(\epsilon\)(strictly positive)
  epsilon_lt_half : epsilon < 1 / 2 -- @realizes \(\epsilon\)(strictly below one half)
  consistency : Consistency Q
  exchangeability : ConditionalExchangeability Q
  overlap : Overlap epsilon (observedMarginal Q)

4d896c8a98332405.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.globalCellValueNonnegative
4d896c8a98332405.statement:
/-- The paper-facing global extension on the nonnegative four-vector cone. -/
noncomputable def globalCellValueNonnegative (epsilon : ℝ)
    (u : NonnegativeCellVector) : ℝ :=
  globalCellValue epsilon u.1

544c53cb47a1eabf.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.oracleValue
544c53cb47a1eabf.statement:
/-- The full-data unrestricted oracle value. -/
noncomputable def oracleValue {d : ℕ} (Q : PotentialLaw d) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x : Fin d, poCellMass Q x * max (poRegression Q 0 x) (poRegression Q 1 x)

471abcd70283ac99.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.identification_and_extension
471abcd70283ac99.statement:
/-- If [the alphabet size satisfies its stated restriction](hyp:hd), and [the overlap parameter satisfies its stated range restriction](hyp:hepsilon), and [the observed law satisfies the stated model restrictions](hyp:hP), then [the observed optimal-value functional is identified and every admissible observed law has a causal completion with the same oracle value](goal). -/
theorem identification_and_extension {d : ℕ} {epsilon : ℝ} (P : DiscreteLaw d)
    (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hepsilon : 0 < epsilon ∧ epsilon < 1 / 2)
    (hP : ObservedModelClass epsilon P) :
    (∀ x, cellVector P x ∈ overlapCone epsilon) ∧
    observedOptimalValue P hP = ∑ x,
      globalCellValueNonnegative epsilon
        ⟨cellVector P x, (cellVector_mem_overlapCone_optimal P hP x).1⟩ ∧
    (∀ u : NonnegativeCellVector,
      0 ≤ globalCellValueNonnegative epsilon u ∧
        globalCellValueNonnegative epsilon u ≤ vectorMass u.1) ∧
    (∀ u v : NonnegativeCellVector,
      |globalCellValueNonnegative epsilon u - globalCellValueNonnegative epsilon v| ≤
        (1 + epsilon⁻¹) * l1CellDistance u.1 v.1) ∧
    (∃ Q : PotentialLaw d,
      CausalCompletionClass epsilon Q ∧ BernoulliCompletionConstruction P Q) ∧
    (∀ Q : PotentialLaw d, CausalCompletionClass epsilon Q →
      ObservedModelClass epsilon (observedMarginal Q))

e13164894f3e5e92.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.causal_optimal_value_corollary
e13164894f3e5e92.statement:
/-- If [the potential-outcome law satisfies the stated causal restrictions](hyp:hQ), then [the causal oracle value equals the optimal value identified from the observed marginal](goal). -/
theorem causal_optimal_value_corollary {d : ℕ} {epsilon : ℝ} (Q : PotentialLaw d)
    (hQ : CausalCompletionClass epsilon Q) :
    oracleValue Q = observedOptimalValue (observedMarginal Q) hQ.observedModel

729fd129e9fc97dc.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.empiricalRatioEstimator
729fd129e9fc97dc.statement:
/-- For [the specified observed sample](hyp:sample), the [empirical-ratio estimator sums empirical cell shares times the larger of the two totalized within-arm success ratios](goal). -/
noncomputable def empiricalRatioEstimator {n d : ℕ} (sample : Fin n → Obs d) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x : Fin d, (sampleCellCount sample x : ℝ) / n *
    max ((sampleSuccessCount sample x false : ℝ) / sampleArmCount sample x false)
      ((sampleSuccessCount sample x true : ℝ) / sampleArmCount sample x true)

100842455ba33735.statement:

c8c80c0338d17bac.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.jacksonTensorPolynomial
c8c80c0338d17bac.statement:
/-- The physical-coordinate polynomial induced by the four-dimensional Jackson convolution. -/
noncomputable def jacksonTensorPolynomial (epsilon : ℝ) (K : ℕ) (hK : 2 ≤ K)
    (Q : Rectangle) (hQ : Q.Valid) (hQ0 : ∀ j, 0 ≤ Q.1 j) : MvPolynomial Cell ℝ :=
  if hepsilon : 0 < epsilon then
    if hQr : ∀ j, 0 < rectangleRadius Q j then
      (Classical.choice (jacksonTensorPolynomialData_exists epsilon K hK Q hQ0 hepsilon hQr)).p
    else
      Classical.choose
        (jacksonTensorPolynomial_degenerate_exists epsilon K hK Q hQ hQ0 hepsilon hQr)
  else 0

c1733177dc300d82.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.jacksonFactorialEstimator
c1733177dc300d82.statement:
/-- For [the specified tuning rule, overlap level, observed sample](hyp:tuning,epsilon,sample), the [Jackson factorial estimator uses the empirical ratio for small alphabets, one half in the saturated regime, and otherwise averages the randomized Jackson statistic over Poisson truncation and fair marks](goal). -/
noncomputable def jacksonFactorialEstimator {n d : ℕ} (tuning : JacksonTuning) (epsilon : ℝ)
    (sample : Fin n → Obs d) : ℝ :=
  if d < tuning.boundedAlphabetCutoff then empiricalRatioEstimator sample
  else if (n : ℝ) < d / logAlphabet d then 1 / 2
  else
    ∫ M : ℕ, (∫ marks : Fin n → Bool,
      jacksonRandomizedStatistic tuning epsilon sample M marks ∂fairMarkLaw n)
      ∂ProbabilityTheory.poissonMeasure (Real.toNNReal (n / 4))

9d0f24d41cc02faf.label: JacksonTuning
9d0f24d41cc02faf.statement:
-- @realizes \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\)(empirical cell ratios)

/-- The named universal tuning constants whose admissible values are chosen by the risk theorem. -/
structure JacksonTuning where
  pilotRadiusConstant : ℝ -- @realizes \(H_0\)(positive universal radius constant)
  jacksonDegreeConstant : ℝ -- @realizes \(\kappa\)(universal constant in (0,1))
  boundedAlphabetCutoff : ℕ -- @realizes \(D_0\)(finite-alphabet cutoff)
  pilotRadiusConstant_pos : 0 < pilotRadiusConstant
  jacksonDegreeConstant_pos : 0 < jacksonDegreeConstant
  jacksonDegreeConstant_lt_one : jacksonDegreeConstant < 1

5f51262c00ab2ed5.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.jackson_factorial_upper
5f51262c00ab2ed5.statement:
/-- If [the product experiment has the stated independent-sampling law](hyp:h_iid), then [the stated jackson factorial upper relation holds](goal). -/
theorem jackson_factorial_upper
    (h_iid : ∀ {d n : ℕ} (P : DiscreteLaw d), IidSampling P (productLaw P n)) :
    ∃ tuning : JacksonTuning, 2 < tuning.boundedAlphabetCutoff ∧
      ∀ epsilon : ℝ, 0 < epsilon → epsilon < 1 / 2 →
      ∃ Cepsilon : ℝ, 0 < Cepsilon ∧ ∀ n d : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → 2 ≤ d →
        ∀ P : DiscreteLaw d, ∀ hP : ObservedModelClass epsilon P,
          Causalean.Stat.sqRisk (productLaw P n) (jacksonFactorialEstimator tuning epsilon)
            (observedOptimalValue P hP) ≤
          Cepsilon * min 1 (d / (n * logAlphabet d))

842441b434283a3b.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.l1Embedding
842441b434283a3b.statement:
/-- For [the specified first probability vector, second probability vector](hyp:Pv,Qv), the [L1 embedding is the potential-outcome law induced by the embedding full-data masses](goal). -/
noncomputable def l1Embedding {d : ℕ} (Pv Qv : ProbabilitySimplex d) : PotentialLaw d :=
  ⟨PMF.ofFintype (fun z => ENNReal.ofReal (l1FullMass Pv Qv z))
    (l1FullMass_nonneg_sum Pv Qv).2⟩
  -- @realizes \(\mathbf P\)(first simplex input) @realizes \(\mathbf Q\)(second simplex input)

set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in

1f6fcf44a7a0945d.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.equal_propensity_l1_reduction
1f6fcf44a7a0945d.statement:
/-- If [the product experiment has the stated independent-sampling law](hyp:h_iid), and [the alphabet size satisfies its stated restriction](hyp:hd), and [the overlap parameter satisfies its stated range restriction](hyp:hepsilon), then [the equal-propensity embedding transfers the paired-distribution L1 minimax lower bound to observed optimal-value estimation](goal). -/
theorem equal_propensity_l1_reduction {n d : ℕ} {epsilon : ℝ}
    (P0 : DiscreteLaw d) (mu_n : MeasureTheory.Measure (Fin n → Obs d))
    (h_iid : IidSampling P0 mu_n) (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    (hepsilon : 0 < epsilon ∧ epsilon < 1 / 2) :
    ∀ Pv Qv : ProbabilitySimplex d,
      let P := observedMarginal (l1Embedding Pv Qv)
      ∃ hP : ObservedModelClass epsilon P,
      (∀ x, cellMass P x = (Pv.1 x + Qv.1 x) / 2) ∧
      (∀ x, 0 < cellMass P x → propensity P x = 1 / 2) ∧
      observedOptimalValue P hP = 1 / 2 + l1Distance Pv Qv / 4 ∧
      l1FixedSampleKernel n d ∘ₘ fixedPairLaw n (Pv, Qv) = productLaw P n ∧
      fixedL1MinimaxRisk n d / 16 ≤ minimaxRisk n d epsilon

b0891cb25a61576b.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.all_estimator_lower
b0891cb25a61576b.statement:
/-- If [the product experiment has the stated independent-sampling law](hyp:h_iid), and [the Cai--Low moment-matching prior result is available](hyp:h_cai_low), and [the Jiao--Han--Weissman Poisson L1 lower bound is available](hyp:h_jhw), then [there is a positive constant, depending only on overlap, for which every estimator has risk at least that constant times the minimum of one and $d/(nlog(ed))$](goal). -/
theorem all_estimator_lower
    (h_iid : ∀ {d n : ℕ} (P : DiscreteLaw d), IidSampling P (productLaw P n))
    (h_cai_low : CaiLowAbsoluteMomentPriors)
    (h_jhw : JhwPoissonL1Lower) :
    ∀ epsilon : ℝ, 0 < epsilon → epsilon < 1 / 2 →
      ∃ cepsilon : ℝ, 0 < cepsilon ∧ ∀ n d : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → 2 ≤ d →
        cepsilon * min 1 (d / (n * logAlphabet d)) ≤ minimaxRisk n d epsilon

28ebdd7bfeb2941b.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.matched_minimax_frontier
28ebdd7bfeb2941b.statement:
/-- If [the Cai--Low moment-matching prior result is available](hyp:h_cai_low_of_gate), and [the Jiao--Han--Weissman Poisson L1 lower bound is available](hyp:h_jhw_of_gate), then [the observed minimax risk is bounded above and below by positive constants times the minimum of one and $d/(nlog(ed))$, with the stated causal and fallback comparisons](goal). -/
theorem matched_minimax_frontier
    (h_cai_low_of_gate : CaiLowAbsoluteMomentPriors)
    (h_jhw_of_gate : JhwPoissonL1Lower) :
    ∃ tuning : JacksonTuning, 2 < tuning.boundedAlphabetCutoff ∧
      ∀ epsilon : ℝ, 0 < epsilon → epsilon < 1 / 2 →
      ∃ cepsilon Cepsilon : ℝ,
        0 < cepsilon ∧ -- @realizes \(c_\epsilon\)(positive lower comparison constant)
        cepsilon ≤ Cepsilon ∧ -- @realizes \(C_\epsilon\)(positive upper constant, since cepsilon is positive)
        ∀ n d : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → 2 ≤ d →
          cepsilon * min 1 (d / (n * logAlphabet d)) ≤ minimaxRisk n d epsilon ∧
          minimaxRisk n d epsilon ≤ jacksonWorstCaseRisk tuning n d epsilon ∧
          jacksonWorstCaseRisk tuning n d epsilon ≤
            Cepsilon * min 1 (d / (n * logAlphabet d)) ∧

268cc3e99df1f1b4.statement:
/-- If [the Cai--Low moment-matching prior result is available](hyp:h_cai_low_of_gate), and [the Jiao--Han--Weissman Poisson L1 lower bound is available](hyp:h_jhw_of_gate), then [observed and causal minimax risks are consistent exactly when $d=o(nlog(en))$, and attain the parametric $1/n$ rate exactly for uniformly bounded alphabets](goal). -/

          IsLittleO atTop (fun n => (dseq n : ℝ))

        (ParametricRate (fun n => minimaxRisk n (dseq n) epsilon) ↔
          BoundedAlphabetSequence dseq) ∧
        (ParametricRate (fun n => causalMinimaxRisk n (dseq n) epsilon) ↔
          BoundedAlphabetSequence dseq)) ∧
      (∀ (dseq : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, 2 ≤ dseq n) →
        (Tendsto (fun n => causalMinimaxRisk n (dseq n) epsilon) atTop (nhds 0) ↔

8aab4d68f3b9d3b9.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.parent_reduction
8aab4d68f3b9d3b9.statement:

        ∃ c C : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ c ≤ C ∧ ∀ n d : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → 2 ≤ d →
          c * min 1 (Real.sqrt d / n + d / (n * Real.log (Real.exp 1 * n))) ≤
            minimaxRisk n d epsilon ∧

          (∃ dmax : ℕ, ∀ n, dseq n ≤ dmax) → EventualParametricRisk epsilon dseq)

        ∃ S : Finset (Cell →₀ ℕ), ∃ coeff : (Cell →₀ ℕ) → ℝ,

          (∀ alpha ∈ S, ∀ j, alpha j ≤ 2 * (K - 1)) ∧

0dbf062e5973a7a9.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.centered_factorial_pilot_control
0dbf062e5973a7a9.statement:
/-- If [the product experiment has the stated independent-sampling law](hyp:h_iid), then [the canonical Jackson tuning simultaneously provides the stated pilot/evaluation laws, factorial moment identities, and uniform bias, variance, and pilot-failure bounds](goal). -/
lemma centered_factorial_pilot_control
    (h_iid : ∀ {d n : ℕ} (P : DiscreteLaw d), IidSampling P (productLaw P n)) :
    ∃ tuning : JacksonTuning, tuning = canonicalJacksonTuning ∧
    ∀ epsilon : ℝ, 0 < epsilon → epsilon < 1 / 2 →
    ∃ Cepsilon : ℝ, 0 < Cepsilon ∧
    ∀ (n d : ℕ) (P : DiscreteLaw d), (hn : 0 < n) → ObservedModelClass epsilon P →
      let m : ℝ := n / 8
      let hm : 0 < m := by exact div_pos (Nat.cast_pos.mpr hn) (by norm_num)
      Measure.map Prod.fst (uncappedMarkedCountLaw n P) =
          ProbabilityTheory.poissonMeasure (Real.toNNReal ((n : ℝ) / 4)) ∧
      Measure.map Prod.snd (uncappedMarkedCountLaw n P) = pilotEvaluationTableLaw m P ∧
      (∀ x : Fin d, Measure.map (fun z => (z.1 x, z.2 x))
          (pilotEvaluationTableLaw m P) = pilotEvaluationLaw m (cellVector P x)) ∧
      (∀ (x : Fin d) (pilot : Cell → ℕ) (j : Cell) (z : ℝ) (h t : ℕ),
        conditionalEvaluationExpectation m (cellVector P x) pilot (fun eval =>
            centeredFactorial m h (eval j) z) = (cellVector P x j - z) ^ h ∧
        conditionalEvaluationExpectation m (cellVector P x) pilot (fun eval =>
            centeredFactorial m h (eval j) z * centeredFactorial m t (eval j) z) =
          ∑ l ∈ Finset.range (min h t + 1),
            (Nat.choose h l : ℝ) * Nat.choose t l * Nat.factorial l *
              (cellVector P x j / m) ^ l *
                (cellVector P x j - z) ^ (h + t - 2 * l)) ∧
      ∀ x : Fin d,
      |cellStatisticExpectation tuning epsilon d m (cellVector P x) hm -
          globalCellValue epsilon (cellVector P x)| ≤
        Cepsilon * (Real.sqrt (cellMass P x / (m * logAlphabet d)) +
          1 / (m * logAlphabet d)) ∧
      cellStatisticVariance tuning epsilon d m (cellVector P x) hm ≤
        Cepsilon * d ^ (1 / 16 : ℝ) *
          (cellMass P x * logAlphabet d / m + logAlphabet d ^ 2 / m ^ 2) ∧
      pilotFailureContribution tuning epsilon d m (cellVector P x) hm ≤
        Cepsilon * (Real.sqrt (cellMass P x / (m * logAlphabet d)) +
          1 / (m * logAlphabet d)) ∧
      pilotFailureSecondMomentContribution tuning epsilon d m (cellVector P x) hm ≤
        Cepsilon * d ^ (1 / 16 : ℝ) *
          (cellMass P x * logAlphabet d / m + logAlphabet d ^ 2 / m ^ 2)

3b68cef058ed236a.label: CausalSmith.Stat.DiscreteOptimalValueMinimaxMatched.denseSubmodel
3b68cef058ed236a.statement:
/-- For [the specified sample size, alphabet size, overlap level, domain certificate, moment-matching prior family](hyp:n,d,epsilon,hdom,priors), the [dense submodel is the moment-matching construction assembled from the dense law, approximation degree, scaled priors, mixtures, target separation, and their certificates](goal). Its components are [the domain certificate](step:1), [the dense law](step:2), [the approximation error](step:3), [the approximation degree](step:4), [the Poisson intensity](step:5), [the dense amplitude](step:6), [the first coordinate prior](step:7), [the second coordinate prior](step:8), [the first scaled product prior](step:9), [the second scaled product prior](step:10), [the first observation mixture](step:11), [the second observation mixture](step:12), [the Poissonized risk](step:13), [the prior target separation](step:14), [the prior conditions](step:15), [the degree identity](step:16), [the target-separation identity](step:17). -/
noncomputable def denseSubmodel (n d : ℕ) (epsilon : ℝ)
    (hdom : DenseConstructionDomain n d epsilon)
    (priors : DensePriorFamily) :
    DenseMomentMatchingConstruction n d epsilon where
  domain := hdom
  law := denseLaw
  approximationError := bestEvenApproxError (lowerDegree d)
  degree := lowerDegree d
  intensity := poissonCellIntensity n d
  amplitude := denseAmplitude n d
  nu0 := priors.nu0 (lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1)
  nu1 := priors.nu1 (lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1)
  prior0 := denseScaledProductPrior n d epsilon hdom
    (priors.nu0 (lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1))
  prior1 := denseScaledProductPrior n d epsilon hdom
    (priors.nu1 (lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1))
  mixture0 := denseObservationMixture n d hdom.1 epsilon hdom
    (priors.nu0 (lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1))
  mixture1 := denseObservationMixture n d hdom.1 epsilon hdom
    (priors.nu1 (lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1))
  poissonizedRisk := poissonOptimalValueRisk (2 * n) d epsilon
  priorMeanSeparation :=
    densePriorTargetMean n d epsilon hdom
      (priors.nu1 (lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1)) -
      densePriorTargetMean n d epsilon hdom
        (priors.nu0 (lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1))
  priorConditions := priors.conditions (lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1)
  degree_eq := rfl
  priorMeanSeparation_eq := by
    let K : EvenDegree := lowerEvenDegree d hdom.1
    have hc := priors.conditions K
    letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (priors.nu0 K) := hc.1
    letI : IsProbabilityMeasure (priors.nu1 K) := hc.2.1
    rw [densePriorTargetMean_formula n d epsilon hdom (priors.nu1 K) hc.2.2.2.1,
      densePriorTargetMean_formula n d epsilon hdom (priors.nu0 K) hc.2.2.1]
    rcases hc with ⟨_hp0, _hp1, _hs0, _hs1, _hy0, _hy1, _hmom, hgap⟩
    have hd0 : (d : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
      exact_mod_cast (Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num) hdom.1))
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul]
    unfold densePriorSeparation
    change _ = denseAmplitude n d * bestEvenApproxError K.1
    field_simp [hd0]
    linear_combination denseAmplitude n d * hgap

b281d1fb038e3870.statement:
/-- If [the product experiment has the stated independent-sampling law](hyp:h_iid), and [the Cai--Low moment-matching prior result is available](hyp:h_cai_low_of_gate), then [in the dense regime, the minimax risk is bounded below by a positive constant times $d/(nlog(ed))$](goal). -/
lemma dense_moment_matching_lower
    (h_iid : ∀ {d n : ℕ} (P : DiscreteLaw d), IidSampling P (productLaw P n))
    (h_cai_low_of_gate : CaiLowAbsoluteMomentPriors) :
    ∃ (D0 : ℕ) (hD0 : 2 ≤ D0), ∀ epsilon : ℝ,
      0 < epsilon → epsilon < 1 / 2 → ∃ cepsilon : ℝ, 0 < cepsilon ∧
      ∀ (d n : ℕ) (hd : D0 ≤ d) (hn : d ^ 2 < n),
        DenseMomentMatchingCertificate D0 d n epsilon cepsilon
